This was a 28-minute call with a self-packing customer; the prep speech was the single highest-value thing he could have given her
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email
Used customer's name only once ('perfect Virginia') — needs 3+
No 60¢/lb baseline coverage mentioned alongside No Worries
top_strength: Outstanding discovery — he probed walk distances at both locations, stairs, disassembly risk, appliances, attic/storage, and let the customer walk her full room-by-room inventory, then translated all of it into a realistic two-day estimate with an honest 'that might be overkill' caveat on the packing hours. The clock explanation was textbook: minimum, prorated increments, and a worked example at 4.5 hours.
coaching_note: Add the Save Your Ass prep speech — this customer is packing herself, is older, and explicitly said she'd forgotten what to rely on a mover for; the consolidation and carload tips would have directly shortened her move and protected the estimate. Also open with a 10-second agenda ('I'll gather details, then walk you through pricing, about 15 minutes — sound good?') so a 28-minute call doesn't feel open-ended.
phone_presence_notes: Genuine warmth and light humor ('You got all the answers, I love it', the CD joke) with the customer volunteering that he'd been 'very thorough' and 'very clear' — held back from a 5 only because he used her name a single time.
